thread:
ben_support: Customer FIN-7891 complaining about sudden p99 spikes on /v1/embeddings from ap-southeast-1 since ~03:00 UTC. They've got user-facing timeouts. Typical p99 ~350ms, now 3s-5s. No errors, just long TLS handshake + tail. Attaching customer probe below.

maria_nw: Thanks Ben. Can you paste the customer's traceroute/tcpdump and region header they send? Any correlation across other customers in the same region?

ben_support: Customer probe (from their VM in ap-southeast-1):
```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (34.120.45.12), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  0.8 ms
 2  isp-edge  3.2 ms
 3  203.119.10.1  25.9 ms
 4  104.16.0.1  45.7 ms
 5  34.120.45.12  3200 ms  <-- big jump
```
They also sent a curl showing TLS handshake times: ClientHello->ServerHello ~2.8s.

anna_ops: I just ran our internal probe from ap-southeast pop to the same customer IP and see intermittent routing via an alternate POP in ap-northeast. Looks like GSLB/EDNS may be resolving to a different POP due to upstream resolver changes. My probe:
```
$ mtr -r -c 10 api.redwood.ai
Host: api.redwood.ai  Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
  1.|-- isp-edge     0.0%     10    0.9   1.1   0.8   2.4   0.5
  2.|-- ap-southeast-pop  0.0%  10  25.2  26.0  24.9  1400  360
```
That huge worst value looks like a cross-region path occasionally chosen.

devon: I dug into TLS metrics on the ingress for that region. We're seeing a burst of retransmits and full handshake retries around the same window. Packet-level shows SYN->SYN/ACK, then a delay, then retransmit. Could be asymmetric routing or MTU path blackhole causing slow completion. Snippet from tcpdump at our pop:
```
12:03:12.123456 IP client->pop: Flags [S], seq 0
12:03:12.124789 IP pop->client: Flags [S.], seq 0
12:03:14.900000 IP client->pop: Flags [ACK], ack 1  <-- big gap
```

sre-bot: [alert] Edge: p99 TLS handshake latency spike detected in ap-southeast-1. Link: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/alerts/EDGE-TSL-4456

maria_nw: If EDNS/ISP resolver changed behavior, customers might get A record pointing to the wrong POP for certain queries. Can we confirm authoritative responses and EDNS client-subnet on the offending queries? Anna, can you capture the DNS responses we return to that resolver? 

anna_ops: Captured response from our authoritative to the customer's resolver: EDNS-client-subnet not present, weight-based GSLB returned ap-northeast endpoint for 8/20 queries. TTL is 60s. Looks like upstream resolver is sharding queries to different anycast clusters, leading to inconsistent routing.

ben_support: Customer asked for a workaround now — they temporarily set a region override header in their requests and saw p99 drop back to ~300ms. Example they used:
```
curl -H "X-Redwood-Region: ap-southeast-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{...}'
```
They want a supported mitigation while we investigate.

maria_nw: Short-term mitigations:
- Ask customer to use region header (documented workaround) — supported as a temporary measure.
- Reduce authoritative TTL to 10s for ap-southeast so we can steer quickly.
- Add a route pin policy in GSLB for the affected resolver subnet to prefer ap-southeast until upstream stabilizes.

devon: Agree. I'll open a rollout to lower TTL and pin route for the resolver's ASN. Also adding TCP keepalive tuning at the pop to reduce handshake stalls.

anna_ops: I'll request ISP traceroutes from our carrier partner and add a packet capture window. Also will run a targeted canary to validate route pinning.

oncall-roster: Owner: devon (networking). ETA for temporary fix: 20 minutes (TTL change + GSLB pin). Postmortem owner: maria_nw. I'll escalate to infra channel if pinning doesn't reduce p99 in 30m.

ben_support: Customer notified, they're applying region header for now and will wait for update. I'll keep the thread posted.

maria_nw: After TTL/pin applied, monitor p95/p99 + TLS handshake retries. If we still see spikes, next step is full peering test and possible pop traffic shift.

devon: TTL change + pin applied (rolled @ 03:25 UTC). Early numbers: p99 from 4.8s -> 420ms for this customer. Will continue monitoring.

ben_support: Customer confirms major improvement. Closing immediate escalation, moving to follow-up investigation. Thanks all :thumbsup:
